**Module 3 objectives**

This module introduces widely used techniques for analysing multivariate biological data. By the end of this module, you will be able to:

- Explain the principles underpinning principal components analysis (PCA), cluster analysis and non-metric multidimensional scaling (nMDS).
- Explain the logic of permutation-based multivariate hypothesis testing, including PERMANOVA and ANOSIM.
- Plan and conduct studies designed to test multivariate hypotheses.
- Perform multivariate analyses using jamovi or R.
- Interpret, present and report the results of multivariate analyses.
:::



## Outline

- **Week 12:** Carry out additional analyses, summarise your findings, and review guidance on describing multivariate methods and results in your report. Demonstrators will provide support with this work.
- **Week 13:** Further support for additional analyses and any remaining work.

During these weeks, we will be in the lab to help with any analyses that groups wish to undertake. This may involve integrating the analyses (e.g. testing the relationships between PCs and univariate measures) or tweaking (not twerking) your analyses by examining subsets of your data using the options available in Jamovi.

## Marking scheme

The marking scheme is included in the Week 9 practical notes and is also available on Canvas, in the Assignments section under **Report 2**.
